choices.label: Buy signal oil (pay 40 cinders; aid the caravan)
choices.resultText: The wick catches. The Road Warden records forty cinders beside Lantern Haven in a weathered supply ledger.

choices.label: Haul the beacon (take 8 damage; aid the caravan)
choices.resultText: The iron frame cuts your palms, but its light clears the ridge. The Road Warden waves Lantern Haven’s wagons through and promises to remember the work.

choices.label: Leave
choices.resultText: You pass the unlit lantern. The caravan must find another way.

view.text:
An unmarked routekeeper braces a broken signal lantern against the rain. The drivers call this traveler the Road Warden; there is no Fell Courtyard crest on the coat.

"That caravan carries medicine to Lantern Haven and the cold hamlets beyond. Oil costs forty cinders. Or help me haul the spare beacon up the scree."
view.title: The Last Lantern

outcome.resultText: The iron frame cuts your palms, but its light clears the ridge. The Road Warden waves Lantern Haven’s wagons through and promises to remember the work.

choices.label: Enter the ring (fight the soldier for 60 cinders)
choices.resultText: You step across the stone line. The soldier finally moves.

choices.label: Circle it instead (lose 5% max HP crossing the rubble, gain 20 cinders)
choices.resultText: The rubble takes its toll, but the ring — and whatever waits in it — stays quiet.

choices.label: Leave
choices.resultText: Some rings are drawn for a reason. You leave this one closed.

view.text: A cracked stone ring marks a trial-ground no map names. A single soldier stands within it, unmoving, waiting for someone foolish or hungry enough to step inside.
view.title: Wyrm Trial

outcome.resultText: You step across the stone line. The soldier finally moves.

view.text: A traveler's pack lies split open at the trail's edge, its owner nowhere to be found. Among the ruined provisions, a single card sits face-down, deliberately placed — as though left as a warning, not a gift.
view.title: Discarded Reliquary

outcome.resultText: You pick it up before you can think better of it. It settles into your deck like it was always there.
